blindReviewDeclaration: I received this checklist in a fresh subagent context, tried to falsify the design, and formed findings and verdict before reading author self-review or author finding disposition.
expectedBehavior: validate-only selects and executes only the declared static set, never Testcontainers, DEV, seed, L2, browser, reset, UAT, or deployment work.
scripts/verify is root metadata only; its eleven GATE leaves and the separate ArchUnit selector have finite, non-recursive, actual-execution receipts.
ACTIVE GATE admission consumes the same successful leaf receipts produced by the root run and rejects missing, extra, substituted, stale, or marker-incomplete receipts.
Assertion disposition occurs per assertion, preserving value and structural truth while retiring only source-text false-red assertions.
A valid-format forged HMAC fails by recomputation at the existing secret-holding boundary without exposing the key, and legacy fixtures are migrated before deletion.
This package remains static-only: it cannot claim dynamic, business, cleanup, performance, Testcontainers, DEV, L2, seed, browser, UAT, or deployment success.

findings.title: The reviewed design is not machine-readable as design-only authority
findings.claim: The manifest correctly declares implementationAuthority=false, but the referenced Markdown design has no parseable implementationAuthority field. Its code-style text is not the authority field required by the existing granularity validator, so the reviewed manifest/design pair cannot pass its declared control.
findings.impact: The design-only boundary is not mechanically bound to the reviewed design. The declared implementation-facing control fails before any delivery unit can be admitted, so no unit can receive a design GO.
findings.minimalRepair: Add the exact parseable design-level implementationAuthority=false declaration required by the existing checker to the design document, preserve the design-only authorization, update the manifest design hash, then rerun the manifest-plus-review checker. Do not weaken the checker or replace this with prose.
findings.denominator: The single design document hash-bound by this manifest and all six THCL delivery units that depend on its design-only authority.
findings.risk: The package's authorization boundary is not enforceable by its already-declared mechanical control.
findings.disposition: Design must be corrected and re-hash-bound before any implementation or downstream review admission.

findings.title: The proposed ACTIVE exact-set has no single-execution receipt transport
findings.claim: The design requires U12 to consume actual root-child receipts, but it does not specify a producer-to-consumer contract or one execution owner. The current verify loop has no receipt collection, while standards-coverage.executeActive independently spawns selected catalog commands and returns only an in-process ref array. Implementing the text as written can either execute the eleven leaves twice or certify a second execution instead of the root run that U12 is meant to admit.
findings.impact: C3 remains false-green-prone: a root run can omit, substitute, or fail a child while an independent U12 re-run supplies a matching ref set. It also violates the required serial first-failure discipline by permitting redundant execution after an earlier leaf result.
findings.minimalRepair: Before implementation, choose and document one receipt owner and one transport: either the root executes every VERIFY_CHILD exactly once and passes immutable per-child {ref, dependency digest, marker result, exit result} receipts to a pure standards-coverage validator, or standards-coverage is the sole leaf executor invoked once by root and returns that exact receipt set. State root receipt consumption, ARCHUNIT_SELECTOR separation, fail-fast behavior, and red mutations for duplicate execution, root-as-child, missing, extra, substituted, stale, and marker-missing receipts.
findings.denominator: 43 ACTIVE GATE rules -> 16 refs: VERIFY_ROOT scripts/verify, 11 VERIFY_CHILD leaf gates, and the separately admitted ARCHUNIT_SELECTOR; no command may be counted twice.
findings.risk: The core C3 receipt semantics are underspecified at the producer/consumer boundary.
findings.disposition: Design must be amended before implementation; retain the existing catalog as the sole map and do not create a parallel control.

findings.title: HMAC reuse is not executable from the identified change surface
findings.claim: The design correctly prohibits format-only HMAC validation and calls for reuse of evidenceHmac plus timingSafeEqual, but the only confirmed existing evidenceHmac/databaseEvidenceHmac implementation is private to backend-performance-final-acceptance.mjs. THCL-U04 neither declares that file nor a shared helper as a change surface, and does not bind a canonical payload/domain for the 196 receipt. A direct import is impossible; copying the private implementation would create the prohibited second implementation.
findings.impact: The B3 forged-but-valid-shape mutation may be addressed by a new divergent HMAC implementation or only at a report-reader layer, leaving the intended secret-holding verification boundary and C3 authenticity claim unclosed.
findings.minimalRepair: Amend THCL-U04 to name the sole reusable HMAC owner and its exact canonical inputs. Declare the smallest source change that exposes a shared, domain-separated verifier or moves the 196 verification to that existing owner; declare the key-owning boundary and a non-secret verification receipt. Add the existing owner and the chosen shared helper, if extracted, to the manifest change surfaces and exact-set red tests for wrong MAC, wrong key, and changed canonical payload.
findings.denominator: Every completion.serverEvidenceHmac and database serverOperationHmac admitted into the 196-row Testcontainers report, plus their existing final-acceptance verifier counterpart.
findings.risk: The required authenticity repair lacks a declared reuse boundary and can regress into a second format-adjacent implementation.
findings.disposition: Design must be amended before implementation; reuse or minimally extract the existing implementation rather than copying it.

solutionReasonableness.problemFit: The design directly targets C1-C4 through the existing verify, catalog, standards checker, test sources, and runners; its refusal to treat static checks as dynamic success fits the authorization boundary.
solutionReasonableness.simplerAlternativeAssessment: A new test-governance framework or broad test glob would add scope and preserve empty-glob or duplicate-control risk. Reusing the catalog and one explicit receipt flow is smaller, but the receipt flow must be made concrete. Likewise, one extracted/reused HMAC verifier is smaller than a second verifier.
solutionReasonableness.costFit: The single serial package is justified by shared C1-C4 control roots and the required migrate-before-delete ordering, but it is only cost-fit after the two cross-unit contracts are made implementation-executable.

conclusion.summary: One confirmed M and two confirmed S findings block design acceptance: the reviewed design is not machine-readable as design-only authority; the C3 exact-set does not yet bind one root execution to one consumed receipt set; and the C3 HMAC repair does not declare an executable reuse boundary for the existing implementation.
conclusion.authorizationBoundary: This is a static DESIGN review only. It neither authorizes nor demonstrates dynamic, business, cleanup, performance, Testcontainers, DEV, L2, reset, seed, browser, UAT, deployment, contract, production, or runner success.
